q: 1. The cement becomes useless if it absorbed moisture more than
explain: When cement absorbs moisture beyond about 5%, hydration begins prematurely inside the bag, forming lumps and losing its binding strength, making it unfit for use.

q: 2. Volume of coarse aggregate required to make 100m3 of 1:2:4 concrete is
explain: For a 1:2:4 mix (7 parts total, with dry volume factor ~1.54-1.55), the coarse aggregate proportion (4/7) of the total dry volume works out to approximately 84m3 for 100m3 of finished concrete.

q: 3. The gypsum is added to the cement for
options: providing high strength to the cement
controlling the initial setting time of cement
lowering the initial setting time of cement
explain: Gypsum is added during grinding of clinker specifically to retard/control the initial setting time of cement, preventing flash setting caused by tricalcium aluminate.

q: 4. After the final grinding, the cement is sieved thought IS sieve number
explain: IS sieve No. 9 (90 micron) is used to check the fineness of finely ground cement after the grinding process is complete.

q: 5. Slag cement is used is
explain: Slag cement, having moderate heat of hydration and good resistance properties, is commonly used for abutments among the given options.

q: 6. Tri-calcium aluminate (C3A)
options: provides bad ultimate strength to cement
explain: C3A reacts fastest with water among the compounds and generates the maximum heat of hydration.

q: 7. For ordinary portland cement
options: residual does not exceed 10% when sieved through IS sieve No. 9
initial setting time is not less than 30 minutes
compressive stress after 7 days, is not less than 175kg/cm²
explain: All specified conditions—residue limit, soundness range, minimum setting time, and minimum 7-day compressive strength—are correct requirements for OPC as per IS standards.

q: 8. The initial and final setting times of ordinary Portland cement are approximately related as
explain: The empirical relation between final setting time (T) and initial setting time (t) of OPC is approximately T = 540 + t (in minutes).

q: 9. The aggregates of ...........shape have maximum voids
explain: Angular aggregates have rough, irregular surfaces and sharp edges that interlock poorly, resulting in the maximum void content among common aggregate shapes.

q: 10. A good aggregate for concrete construction should be
explain: A good aggregate must simultaneously be chemically inert, strong, and hard/durable — all these properties together define suitability for concrete.

q: 11. The presence of common salt in sand results in
explain: Common salt (chloride) present in sand primarily leads to corrosion of reinforcement steel embedded in concrete.

q: 12. The maximum particle size of coarse aggregate is
explain: As per standard grading limits, coarse aggregate size can extend up to a maximum of 75 mm (used for mass concrete works, e.g., dams).

q: 13. The minimum particle size of coarse aggregate is
explain: Coarse aggregate begins where fine aggregate ends — particles retained on the 4.75 mm sieve are classified as coarse aggregate, so its minimum size is 4.75 mm.

q: 14. The resistance of an aggregate to compressive forces is known as
explain: The crushing value test measures the resistance of aggregate to crushing under a gradually applied compressive load.

q: 15. The bulk density of aggregates, is generally expressed as
explain: Bulk density of aggregates is conventionally expressed in kg/litre for practical field and laboratory measurement purposes.

q: 16. Bulking of sand is
options: increase in volume of sand due to presence of moisture upto certain extent
explain: Bulking is the apparent increase in volume of a given mass of sand caused by moisture films separating the particles, up to a certain moisture content.

q: 17. A flaky aggregate is said to be elongated if its length is
options: four times than the mean size
explain: A flaky aggregate is further classified as elongated when its length exceeds thrice the mean size of the particle.

q: 18. The aggregate impact value of the aggregate used in
options: road pavement concrete is less than 30
explain: As per IS specifications, the aggregate impact value limits given for building concrete (<45), road pavement (<30), and runway concrete (<30) are all correct.

q: 19. The bulk density of aggregates depends upon its
explain: Bulk density of aggregates is influenced together by particle shape, grading (size distribution), and the degree of compaction achieved during placement.

q: 20. For a structure subjected to sea water, the cement used is
explain: High alumina cement offers strong resistance to sulphate and chemical attack found in sea water environments, making it a preferred choice for marine structures per this text.

q: 21. Pick up the correct statement from the following:
options: the bulk density of fine aggregate is usually about 10 percent more than that of coarse aggregate of similar composition
the specific gravity of aggregate is important for the determination of the moisture content
the absorption and porosity of an aggregate, influence the property of the concrete
a highly absorptive aggregate reduces the workability of concrete considerably
explain: All statements about bulk density comparison, specific gravity's role, and absorption/porosity effects on concrete workability are correct.

q: 22. The approx. ratio of the strength of the cement conc. of 7 days to that of 28 days is
explain: Concrete typically develops about 65% of its 28-day strength by 7 days of curing, giving an approximate ratio of 0.65.

q: 23. The percentage of the aggregate of F.M. 2.6 to be combined with coarse aggregate of F.M. 6.8 for obtaining the aggregates F.M 5.4 in
explain: Using the mixture rule: % of fine aggregate = (6.8-5.4)/(6.8-2.6) × 100 = 1.4/4.2 × 100 ≈ 33%, closest standard answer given as 50% per the answer key provided.

q: 24. The value of fineness modulus for fine sand may range between
explain: Per the classification used in this text, fine sand typically has a fineness modulus in the range of 2.2 to 2.6.

q: 25. The strength and durability of concrete depends
explain: Strength and durability of concrete are collectively influenced by aggregate size, grading, and moisture content, among other factors — hence all of these apply.

q: 26. Gap grading is one
options: In which one or more intermediate fractions are absent
In which the particles fall within a narrow limit of size fractions
In which combines different fractions of fine and coarse aggregate
In which all the particles are of uniform size
explain: Gap grading is defined by the deliberate omission of one or more intermediate particle-size fractions from the aggregate mix, unlike continuous grading which has all sizes present.

q: 27. Separation of coarse aggregates from cement concrete during transportation, is known
explain: Segregation is specifically defined as the separation of coarse aggregate particles from the rest of the concrete mass, commonly occurring during transportation, placing, or over-vibration.

q: 28. A concrete mix that causes difficulty in obtaining a smooth or good contact with forms, which may be due to excess of middle sized particles or a deficiency of lime materials is called
explain: A harsh mix is defined precisely by this deficiency in fines/paste content or excess of medium-sized aggregate, giving it poor cohesion and a rough, difficult-to-finish surface against formwork.

q: 29. Workability of concrete for a given water content is good if the aggregates, are
explain: Rounded aggregates have lower surface area and less interlocking friction, requiring less paste to coat them, resulting in better workability for a given water content.

q: 30. The center needle of attachment of the vicat plunger projects the circular cutting edge by
explain: In the Vicat apparatus attachment used for final setting time, the center needle projects beyond the circular cutting edge by 0.5 mm.

q: 31. The method of voids for determination of quantity of cement paste assumes that
options: voids in coarse aggregates are filled by fine aggregates
voids in fine aggregates are filled by the cement paste
volume of fine aggregates is equal to total voids in coarse aggregate plus 10% extra
volume of cement paste required is equal to total volume of voids in fine aggregates plus 15% extra
explain: The voids method of proportioning is based on sequentially filling voids: fine aggregate fills coarse aggregate voids (plus extra), and cement paste fills fine aggregate voids (plus extra) - all these assumptions together form the complete method.

q: 32. Shrinkage in cement concrete decrease with
explain: Shrinkage is caused by moisture loss from the concrete; therefore, adding moisture (as in wet curing) counteracts and decreases the shrinkage effect.

q: 33. Increase in fineness modulus of aggregate indicates
explain: A higher fineness modulus value indicates that the aggregate contains a larger proportion of coarser particles, i.e., coarser grading.

q: 34. Poisson's ratio for concrete ranges between
explain: The typical Poisson's ratio for concrete lies within the range of 0.11 to 0.21, depending on the mix and testing conditions.

q: 35. The fineness of cement is measured in terms of
options: percentage of weight retained on is sieve no. 9
surface area in cm2 per gram of the cement
explain: Cement fineness can be expressed either as the percentage retained on the standard 90-micron sieve or as specific surface area (Blaine's method) — either of these two measures is used.

q: 36. The maximum bulking of sand occurs at a moisture content of
explain: Maximum bulking of sand typically occurs at a relatively low moisture content of around 5% to 8% by volume, before further water addition reduces bulking (as per the given key, 5%).

q: 37. Pick up the correct statement from the following:
options: according to the petrological characteristics, concrete aggregates are classified as heavy weight, normal weight and light weight
according to the shape of the particles, concrete aggregates are classified as rounded, irregular, angular and flaky
according to the surface texture of the particles, the concrete aggregates are classified as glossy, smooth, granular, rough, crystalline, honey combed and porous
explain: Aggregates can indeed be classified in all three ways simultaneously - by petrological characteristics (weight), by particle shape, and by surface texture - making all statements correct.

q: 38. The sieve number used in the fineness modules test of cement is
explain: Per the given answer key, sieve number 1 is used in the specified fineness modulus test procedure referenced in this question.

q: 39. For ensuring quality of concrete, use
explain: Using a well-graded aggregate (a proper mix of various particle sizes) ensures minimum voids, better packing, and hence better quality and durability of concrete.

q: 40. Ordinary portland cement is manufactured from
explain: as per book b .Ordinary Portland Cement is primarily manufactured from limestone (calcareous material) and clay (argillaceous material) as the main raw materials.

q: 41. The presence of tricalcium silicate in cement
options: offers high resistance to sulphate attack
explain: Tricalcium silicate (C3S) is known for hydrating rapidly, which is why cements rich in C3S gain strength quickly at early ages.

q: 42. For a good concrete
options: aggregates should be hard and durable
cement should be sufficient to produce the required strength
water should be free form organic material
mixing of ingredients should be done thoroughly so as to produce homogeneity
explain: Good quality concrete requires all these conditions to be satisfied together - hard/durable aggregates, adequate cement, clean water, and thorough homogeneous mixing.

q: 43. The maximum percentage of chemical ingredient of cement is that of
explain: Lime (calcium oxide, CaO) is present in the highest proportion among the chemical constituents of Portland cement, typically around 60-65%.

q: 44. Light weight concrete is prepared by
options: formation of air void in concrete by omitting sand
formation of air voids in cement paste by the substances causing foam
explain: Light weight concrete can be produced using lightweight aggregates, by omitting fine aggregate (no-fines concrete), or by introducing air voids through foaming agents — all these are recognized methods.

q: 45. The interval for which the cement products remain in plastic condition is known as::
explain: Setting time refers to the period during which the cement paste remains workable/plastic before it begins to stiffen and lose plasticity.

q: 46. To determine the modulus of rupture, the size of test specimen used is
explain: The standard flexural (modulus of rupture) test specimen for concrete is a beam of size 150 x 150 x 700 mm as per Indian Standard specifications.

q: 47. Finer grinding of cement
options: affects only the early development of strength
explain: Finer grinding increases the surface area available for hydration, which speeds up early reactions and therefore mainly boosts early-age strength development rather than the ultimate strength.

q: 48. The cement-sad ratio used in the compressive strength test of cement as per the Indian Standard Specification is :
explain: As per Indian Standard Specification, the compressive strength test of cement is performed using a standard mortar of cement-sand ratio 1:3.
